intended_object: The canonical R-linear map M* → Hom^C(M, C), from the linear dual of a right C-comodule M to comodule morphisms into the regular right comodule C. It sends φ to the matrix-coefficient morphism m ↦ (φ ⊗ id)(ρ(m)). This is the map behind the cofree-comodule adjunction Hom^C(M, C) ≅ M*. I took this from the docstring, the module documentation and the name.
explanation:
The definition bundles `matrixCoefficientHom` as an R-linear map in φ. That function sends φ to the comodule morphism whose underlying linear map is `lid ∘ (φ ⊗ id) ∘ coact`, i.e. m ↦ Σ φ(m₀) m₁. Additivity and R-linearity in φ come from the lemmas just above it in the file, so the map is the standard one: M* → Hom^C(M, C), φ ↦ (φ ⊗ id) ∘ ρ.

The setting is already as general as it should be: a commutative semiring R, any R-coalgebra C and any right C-comodule M. The free and finite hypotheses on M are introduced only in later sections, so they do not apply here.

Mathlib, at the commit used, has no comodules and no matrix coefficients. My searches for `class Comodule`, `structure Comodule` and `matrixCoeff` found nothing, so there is no more general Mathlib version to point to. The definition is faithful.
